'''''The Indispensability of Mathematics'''''<ref>{{Cite book |last=Colyvan |first=Mark |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OBs-TSFopLkC |title=The Indispensability of Mathematics |publisher=Oxford University Press |year=2001 |isbn=978-0-19-513754-5 |edition=1 |location=New York |language=en |doi=10.1093/019513754x.001.0001}}</ref> is a 2001 book by [[Mark Colyvan]] in which he examines the [[Quine–Putnam indispensability argument]] in the [[philosophy of mathematics]]. This thesis is based on the premise that mathematical entities are placed on the same ontological foundation as other theoretical entities indispensable to our best [[scientific theories]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Melia |first1=Joseph |title=Mark Colyvan, The Indispensability of Mathematics. |journal=Metascience |date=March 2003 |volume=12 |issue=1 |pages=55–58 |doi=10.1023/A:1024411117330 |s2cid=169768062 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cole |first1=J. |title=Review: The Indispensability of Mathematics |journal=Mind |date=1 March 2003 |volume=112 |issue=446 |pages=331–336 |doi=10.1093/mind/112.446.331 |url=https://academic.oup.com/mind/article-abstract/112/446/331/990943 |accessdate=26 October 2018 |language=en |issn=0026-4423|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cheyne |first1=C. |title=The Indispensability of Mathematics |journal=Australasian Journal of Philosophy |date=September 2002 |volume=80 |issue=3 |pages=378–379 |doi=10.1080/713659474 |s2cid=170188260 |language=en |issn=0004-8402}}</ref>
